title: The Czech November rate decision lifts the repo rate to 4.00%
summary: The CNB raised the two-week repo rate by 25 basis points to 4.00% on November 5. It also increased the discount rate to 3.00% and the Lombard rate to 5.00% by the same amount. The changes moved the corridor upward in parallel, with the repo rate one percentage point from each boundary.

The new rates took effect on November 6. Distinguish the public decision on November 5 from its application to central-bank operations the next day. A surprise in financial prices depends on what was expected before the 14:30 announcement, while the later press conference provides a separate information event. The initial notice confirms the instrument changes and effective date without supplying the vote or rationale.

questions.question: How much of the 25-basis-point increase was unexpected?
questions.detail: Compare the expected pre-release repo rate with 4.00%, adjusting derivatives for the effective date and any remaining days before the new rate applies.

questions.question: Did the short end and the koruna respond at the same time?
questions.detail: Use synchronized executable quotes after 14:30 but before the later press conference, checking foreign rates and currency moves over the same interval.

questions.question: How did overnight implementation compare with the new corridor?
questions.detail: Observe the effective market rate on November 6 relative to the 3.00%, 4.00% and 5.00% settings. Keep the operational response distinct from the previous day’s information surprise.
